title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, resource Sharing] How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] Can you explain: how do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, eviction Defense] A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?

Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Look, Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Dogs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Dogs] What if the police bring out K9 units to intimidate us?

Stay calm and don't make sudden movements or run, which can trigger the dog's training to chase and bite. Keep your hands visible and tucked away from the animal's reach. Remember that these dogs are being used as weapons by a system that doesn't care about their safety or yours; stay focused on the human handlers. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, internal Conflict] What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?

Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition Building] A friend asked me: 'How do I bring different groups together for one campaign?' What do I tell them?

Find the common enemy: the developers, the corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who serve them. Show the environmentalists that their fight is the same as the housing advocates' fight, because the same people are destroying the air and the neighborhood. Build the campaign around a 'People’s Charter' that reflects the shared needs of the entire working class. Unity isn't about everyone agreeing on everything; it's about everyone fighting the same fight together.

title: Karl Organizing: Signal Apps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signal Apps] How should we communicate during the actual protest?

Use Signal with disappearing messages set to one hour or less to keep your plans off the state's servers. Avoid using voice calls on the open airwaves because the cops have 'stingrays' that can intercept your location and your data. Keep the group chats focused on logistics—water, police movement, and route changes—and save the theory for the post-protest debrief.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: long-term Planning] Give me the short version: How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: labor Endorsements] Give me the short version: How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Gardens
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Gardens] The city says our neighborhood garden is illegal. Should we stop?

Here's the thing: Keep planting and get the whole block to help you defend that dirt. Guerrilla gardening is an act of defiance against a system that wants us dependent on corporate grocery chains. If they try to bulldoze it, make sure there's a crowd there to stop them and a camera to record the state destroying a source of food. A plot of land that feeds people is more sacred than any zoning law written by a bureaucrat.

title: Karl Organizing: Banner Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Banner Making] What's the best way to make a banner that people can actually see?

Use high-contrast colors like black on yellow or white on red, and keep the font thick and blocky. Don't try to write a manifesto on a piece of cardboard; three to five words is the sweet spot for a camera to catch. Use PVC pipe or sturdy wood for the poles, and make sure two people are assigned to each banner so it stays taut and readable even in a breeze.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: emergency Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: emergency Funds] Give me the short version: How do we handle fundraising for bail or legal defense?

This is where speed and trust matter most. Use encrypted channels to blast out the need to your most dedicated supporters the second a comrade is snatched. Keep these funds strictly segregated from your operating budget so that when the hammer drops, you can move instantly to get our people back on the streets where they belong.

title: Karl Organizing: Safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safe Zones] A friend asked me: 'How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, cop Watch Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, cop Watch Safety] Is it legal to film the police when they're making an arrest?

It is your right, but the pigs don't care about the law, so stay back at least ten feet and keep your hands visible. Use an app that uploads footage instantly to the cloud so they can't delete the evidence if they snatch your phone. Don't yell or interfere physically; just keep that lens steady and be the witness our comrades need. Your footage is the only thing that keeps their lies from becoming the official story.

title: Karl Organizing: Escrow Accounts
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Escrow Accounts] Where should we put the money during a rent strike?

You need a neutral place where the landlord can't touch it, like a collective escrow account handled by a lawyer or a trusted member of your union. Don't just leave it in your personal checking account where you might accidentally spend it on groceries. Tell the landlord in writing that the money is sitting there waiting for them, but they only get the keys to the vault once the mold is gone and the elevators work. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowd Logistics] How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying leaders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying leaders] Who should I recruit for the organizing committee first?

Stop looking for the loudest person and start looking for the most respected one. You want the worker that everyone goes to when they have a problem or a question. If you get the natural leaders on board, the rest of the crew will follow because they trust their peers more than any suit. Build your committee with a leader from every single department and shift. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rotating Roles] Can you explain: should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?

Here's how it works: Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action Support] How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

Here's the thing: You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] Can you explain: how should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?

Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant Union Ties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant Union Ties] A friend asked me: 'Should my campaign be linked to the local tenant union?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely. The tenant union is the backbone of working-class power in the city. Their struggle is your struggle, and your campaign should be a vehicle for their demands. When you win, you’re not just a politician; you’re an extension of their movement inside the government. Use your platform to amplify their strikes and their demands for universal rent control and the right to counsel in eviction court.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, community Fridge Startup] How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors] One neighbor is a suck-up to the landlord and tells them everything we do. What do we do?

Don't waste energy attacking them, but freeze them out of the strategy meetings. Continue winning improvements for the whole building; when that neighbor sees their own rent stay flat or their repairs get done because of the union's work, their loyalty to the parasite will crumble. Success is the best recruitment tool for the skeptical and the scared.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: bail Funds] Give me the short version: What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] Can you explain: how can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, house Parties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, house Parties] How do we make a house party fundraiser actually successful?

Here's the thing: Keep the speeches short and the energy high. You want people to feel the heat of the movement, not sit through a boring lecture. Have a clear, bold 'ask' halfway through the night, pass a physical bucket, and make sure everyone knows exactly what fight that money is going toward before the music starts back up.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant Organizing] The landlord won't fix my leaking roof. How do I get them to move?

Karl's answer: Stop acting alone and go talk to your neighbors to see who else is getting screwed by this vulture. Form a tenant union and send a collective demand letter with everyone's signature and a hard deadline. If they don't fix it, prepare to pool your rent in an escrow account to show that the money stops until the repairs start.

title: Karl Organizing: Red Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Red Lines] How do we know when a compromise is actually a sell-out?

If the deal helps the bosses more than the workers, or if it throws one part of your coalition under the bus to save the rest, it’s a sell-out. Never trade the rights of one group for a tiny raise for another; that’s how the ruling class divides us. A real win leaves your coalition stronger and more united for the next fight, not fractured and suspicious.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, physical Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, physical Training] Do we need to learn how to fight for community defense?

It’s better to have the skills and not need them than to be helpless when a fascist or a rogue cop gets physical. Host basic self-defense or de-escalation classes in your backyard or a local gym. Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] Can you explain: what is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: surveillance Awareness] Give me the short version: How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Observers] Can you explain: who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?

Here's the thing: Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: Scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Scaling Up] Can you explain: how do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?

Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack.

title: Karl Organizing: Mold and Health
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mold and Health] There's black mold in my kid's room and the landlord says it's just 'dirt.' What do I do?

Get a professional inspection and a doctor's note linking the mold to health issues immediately. This isn't a 'maintenance request' anymore; it's a liability nightmare for the landlord. Use that documentation to demand an immediate professional abatement and a rent abatement for the time you've lived in toxic conditions. If they refuse, the union goes to the health department together. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Skillshare Organization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skillshare Organization] A friend asked me: 'I want to teach people how to fix bikes, but I've never organized a workshop before.' What do I tell them?

Look, Grab your tools, find a public park or a community center, and put up some flyers with a clear time and date. Keep it hands-on and skip the long lectures—people learn best by doing, not by listening to us talk. Make sure the space is accessible to everyone and encourage those who learn quickly to start helping the newcomers. We're breaking the monopoly on knowledge that the bosses use to keep us dependent and helpless.

title: Karl Organizing: Long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Long-term Planning] How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Here's how it works: Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: Secret organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secret organizing] Why do we have to keep our union talk a secret at first?

Loose lips get comrades fired. If the boss finds out you're organizing before you have a solid core of supporters, they'll pick you off one by one for 'performance issues' or some other lie. You keep it underground to build your strength in the shadows. Once you've got the numbers, you come out as a united front that's too big to crush. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Donor Capture] Can you explain: a wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Look, Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, benefit Events] We want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Here's the thing: Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition Building] How do we get different groups in the city to work together?

Karl's answer: Stop arguing over every minor theory point and focus on a single, concrete goal that helps everyone, like stopping a new jail or raising the minimum wage. Show up for their actions before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidarity is built through shared sweat and trust, not long meetings about manifestos. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, secure Document Sharing] Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?

It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, campaign Literature
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, campaign Literature] What should my flyers look like?

Here's the thing: Bold, clear, and high-contrast. No small print and no flowery language. Put your face on there so people know you're a neighbor, and list three concrete things you will do on Day One to make their lives easier. Use union printers and include the bug to show you support organized labor. Every flyer should have a clear call to action: join the fight, chip in to pool resources, or show up at the polls.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, reaching the Unorganized] How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Security] Can the police track me through my Bluetooth?

Here's the thing: Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass.

title: Karl Organizing: Code Enforcement
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Code Enforcement] The city inspector never does anything. How do we get them to actually fine the landlord?

Here's the thing: One call is a nuisance; thirty calls in one morning is a crisis. Coordinate your union to flood the code enforcement line all at once so the city can't ignore the volume. When the inspector shows up, have a committee of tenants ready to walk them through every unit to point out the rot they usually 'miss.' Don't let them leave until they've written a citation for every single violation they saw.

title: Karl Organizing: Grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grant Alternatives] Can you explain: foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowdfunding Platforms] Which website should we use to raise money online?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] A friend asked me: 'Is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?' What do I tell them?

Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: Transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transit Policy] What's the radical approach to local transit?

Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people.

title: Karl Organizing: Political Education
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Political Education] Should we charge for our reading groups and pamphlets?

Cover your costs, but never turn a profit on knowledge. Charge enough for the physical books or zines to fund the next print run, and always have a 'pay what you can' stack for comrades who are broke. Our goal is to arm the working class with ideas, not to gatekeep the revolution behind a paywall. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Slumlord Intimidation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Slumlord Intimidation] My landlord is threatening to call ICE or the police because we're organizing. What do I do?

This is a classic scare tactic from a coward. Document every threat, record every call, and immediately blast their behavior on social media and to local reporters. When a landlord threatens your safety, you move the fight from the hallway to the public square. Reach out to local immigrant rights groups and ensure your union has a 'no-knock' policy where neighbors look out for each other at the door. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: ethical Banking] Give me the short version: Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, surveillance Awareness] How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

Real talk: You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: Marshals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Marshals] What exactly are marshals supposed to do during the march?

Marshals are the backbone of our safety, keeping the crowd together and buffering us from traffic or hostile agitators. They are not cops; they don't boss comrades around, they facilitate the flow and watch the flanks for snatch squads. Give them high-vis vests and clear communication tools so they can spot trouble before it reaches the heart of our movement.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] What's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Here's the thing: Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: bail Fund Priorities
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: bail Fund Priorities] Give me the short version: Our bail fund is small. How do we decide who to get out of jail first?

Let me break it down: Prioritize the comrades most at risk: trans folks, people with urgent medical needs, and parents who might lose their kids if they miss a day of work. We aren't here to play judge or jury; we're here to snatch our neighbors back from the state's kidnapping machine. Get those who are facing the longest pre-trial stretches out first so they can fight their cases from a position of strength. Every person we free is a middle finger to the carceral state.

title: Karl Organizing: Mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mapping Vulnerability] Can you explain: how do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?

Let me break it down: Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be.

title: Karl Organizing: Long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Long-term Planning] Can you explain: how do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: Burnout prevention
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burnout prevention] How do I avoid burning out as an organizer?

Rest is a tactic, not a luxury. Set real boundaries — the work will take everything you give it and ask for more. Build a bench so nothing depends on one person. Celebrate wins, even small ones. And find joy outside the fight; a movement of exhausted martyrs doesn't last. Take the break. We'll hold the line.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections. Start today.
